---
title: getLedgers
description: Returns list of ledgers
---

{/* rpc-method: generated from the OpenRPC spec */}

The `getLedgers` method returns a detailed list of ledgers starting from the user specified starting point that you can paginate as long as the pages fall within the history retention of their corresponding RPC provider.

## Params (3)

<Tip>
Please note that parameter structure within the request must contain named parameters as a by-name object, and not as positional arguments in a by-position array
</Tip>

<ParamField body="startLedger" type="number">
  Ledger sequence number to start fetching responses from (inclusive). This method will return an error if `startLedger` is less than the oldest ledger stored in this node, or greater than the latest ledger seen by this node. If a cursor is included in the request, `startLedger` must be omitted.
  
  Sequence number of the ledger.
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="pagination" type="object">
  Pagination in stellar-rpc is similar to pagination in Horizon. See [Pagination](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/data/rpc/api-reference/structure/pagination).
  <Expandable title="properties">
    <ParamField body="cursor" type="string">
      An opaque string which acts as a paging token. To obtain the next page of results occurring after a given response set this value to the `cursor` field of the response.
    </ParamField>
    <ParamField body="limit" type="number">
      The maximum number of records returned. The limit for getLedgers can range from 1 to 200 - an upper limit that is hardcoded in Stellar-RPC for performance reasons. If this argument isn't designated, it defaults to 50.
    </ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

<ParamField body="xdrFormat" type="string">
  Lets the user choose the format in which the response should be returned - either as unpacked JSON or as base64-encoded XDR strings. Note that you should not rely on any schema for the JSON, as it will change when the underlying XDR changes.
  
  Specifies whether XDR should be encoded as Base64 (default or 'base64') or JSON ('json').
</ParamField>

## Result

*(getLedgersResult)*

<ResponseField name="ledgers" type="object[]">
  <Expandable title="items">
    <ResponseField name="hash" type="string">
      The hash of the ledger header which was included in the chain
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="sequence" type="number">
      The sequence number of the ledger (sometimes called the 'block height').
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="ledgerCloseTime" type="string">
      The unix timestamp (as a string) at which the ledger was closed.
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="headerXdr" type="string">
      The [LedgerHeaderHistoryEntry](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/blob/v26.0/Stellar-ledger.x#L277) structure for this ledger (base64-encoded string).
    </ResponseField>
    <ResponseField name="metadataXdr" type="string">
      The [LedgerCloseMeta](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-xdr/blob/v22.0/Stellar-ledger.x#L539) union for this ledger (base64-encoded string).
    </ResponseField>
  </Expandable>
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="latestLedger" type="number">
  The sequence number of the latest ledger known to Stellar RPC at the time it handled the request.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="latestLedgerCloseTime" type="number">
  The unix timestamp of the close time of the latest ledger known to Stellar RPC at the time it handled the request.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="oldestLedger" type="number">
  The sequence number of the oldest ledger ingested by Stellar RPC at the time it handled the request.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="oldestLedgerCloseTime" type="number">
  The unix timestamp of the close time of the oldest ledger ingested by Stellar RPC at the time it handled the request.
</ResponseField>

<ResponseField name="cursor" type="string">
  A token which can be included in a subsequent request to obtain the next page of results.
</ResponseField>

## Example

Query a list of ledgers starting from the given startLedger.

**Request**

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -X POST \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 8675309,
  "method": "getLedgers",
  "params": {
    "startLedger": 36233,
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 2
    }
  }
}' \
https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org | jq
```

```js JavaScript
let requestBody = {
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 8675309,
  "method": "getLedgers",
  "params": {
    "startLedger": 36233,
    "pagination": {
      "limit": 2
    }
  }
}
let res = await fetch('https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  },
  body: JSON.stringify(requestBody),
})
let json = await res.json()
console.log(json)
```

```python Python
import json, requests
res = requests.post("https://soroban-testnet.stellar.org", json={
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 8675309,
    "method": "getLedgers",
    "params": {
        "startLedger": 36233,
        "pagination": {
            "limit": 2
        }
    }
})
print(json.dumps(res.json(), indent=4))
```

### Using the Lab

You can retrieve a list of **past ledgers** using the `getLedgers` method in the [Stellar Laboratory](https://laboratory.stellar.org). This endpoint returns detailed ledger data starting from a specified point, with support for pagination—as long as the requested range falls within the history retention of the RPC provider.

The method also supports an optional `XDR format` parameter, which allows developers to choose between **unpacked JSON** or **base64-encoded XDR strings** for the response format.

👉 [View getLedgers on the Lab](https://lab.stellar.org/endpoints/rpc/get-ledgers?$=network$id=testnet&label=Testnet&horizonUrl=https:////horizon-testnet.stellar.org&rpcUrl=https:////soroban-testnet.stellar.org&passphrase=Test%20SDF%20Network%20/;%20September%202015;&endpoints$params$startLedger=573041&xdrFormat=json;;)
